title: Base ideal and boundary colength of a nodal linear series
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Let $L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $V\subseteq H^0(X,L)$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-subspace containing a section nonzero at every component generic point [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Define $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ by $L\otimes\mathcal B=\operatorname{im}(V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to L)$, the evaluation image [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\mathcal B$ is a coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], its closed subscheme $Z$ is zero-dimensional, and $b=\dim_k\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is finite. If $\mathcal P$ is a partition of the irreducible components such that $V$ is the direct sum of its subspaces consisting of sections supported on the respective blocks (support here means vanishing at every component generic point outside the block), let $E_{\mathcal P}$ be the reduced finite subscheme consisting of nodes joining two different blocks. For each block $A$, its scheme-theoretic intersection with the reduced union of the other blocks is a disjoint union of reduced $k$-points, precisely the nodes on that boundary; its $k$-length is their number [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $\mathcal B\subseteq I_{E_{\mathcal P}}$ and $b\ge |E_{\mathcal P}|$, the number of those nodes [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].
If $V=H^0(X,L)$, the inclusion induces $H^0(X,L\otimes\mathcal B)=H^0(X,L)$ inside $H^0(X,L)$. If moreover $L=I_T\otimes\omega_X$ for an effective Cartier zero-dimensional subscheme $T$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch], the coherent product ideal $I_{\bar T}=I_T\mathcal B$ defines a zero-dimensional subscheme $\bar T\supseteq T$ satisfying
$$\ell(\bar T)=\ell(T)+b,\qquad H^0(X,I_{\bar T}\otimes\omega_X)=H^0(X,I_T\otimes\omega_X),$$
where $\ell(U)=\dim_k\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$.

proof.text: Projectivity implies properness. The proper-field preparation gives that $X$ is Noetherian and $L$ and $\mathcal O_X$ are coherent. Choose a basis $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ of $V$. On an affine open trivializing $L$, write $s_i=f_i e$. Then $\mathcal B$ is the ideal $(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$; changing $e$ multiplies all generators by a unit, so these local ideals glue to the stated evaluation ideal. More intrinsically it is the image of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus d}\to L$, tensored by $L^{-1}$. The coherence lemma gives coherence of the finite sum, its cokernel, and the kernel of $L\to\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm{ev})$, hence of the image. Tensoring by a line is locally the identity, so $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal B$ are coherent.

source.place: Tag 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), coherence of finite sums, kernels and cokernels; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian)

proof.text: Let $s\in V$ be nonzero at every component generic point. At such a point the reduced local ring is a field, so $s$ generates $L$ there and $\mathcal B_\eta=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$. Thus $Z=V(\mathcal B)$ misses all component generic points and is nowhere dense. Apply the dimension-drop node to this closed subscheme of the finite-type scheme $X$ of dimension one. It gives $\dim Z\le0$, and the finite-subscheme node gives that $Z$ is affine and $b=\dim_k\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is finite. The empty scheme is allowed throughout.

For a block $A$, give its component union and its complementary union $C$ their reduced structures. They are reduced closed subschemes of pure dimension one when nonempty. The scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus A$ is $C$: on a reduced affine chart, a function vanishes on that open precisely when it vanishes in the domains at all complementary component generic points; intersecting their minimal prime ideals is the ideal of $C$. Apply the closed-subcurve node with $Y=A$. Its hypotheses hold because $X$ is finite type, reduced, pure one-dimensional, and has the specified split completed nodes; $k$ algebraically closed makes the residue extensions trivial. It gives $A\times_X C$ as a finite disjoint union of reduced $k$-points, all nodes. Its underlying set is exactly the points lying on a component in $A$ and one outside $A$, hence exactly this block's boundary nodes. Its section algebra is the product of one copy of $k$ per point, proving the asserted boundary length. For a single block the complement and boundary are empty. Taking the union over the finitely many blocks gives the finite reduced subscheme $E_{\mathcal P}$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), (2)(a),(b) and its minimal-prime description of complementary subcurves

proof.text:
For $v_A\in V$ supported on a block $A$, its restriction to the reduced complementary union is zero: in a local trivialization each coefficient vanishes in all component fraction fields of that union, so lies in the intersection of its minimal primes, which is zero. At a node joining two different blocks, every summand $v_A$ therefore has zero residue (at least one incident component is outside $A$). Since $V$ is the sum of these subspaces, every $v\in V$ has zero residue at each such node. The local generators $f_i$ of $\mathcal B$ consequently lie in its maximal ideal. As $E_{\mathcal P}$ is reduced, its ideal is exactly the kernel of restriction to these residue fields. Hence $\mathcal B\subseteq I_{E_{\mathcal P}}$. In the coherent exact sequence
$$0\to I_{E_{\mathcal P}}/\mathcal B\to\mathcal O_X/\mathcal B\to\mathcal O_{E_{\mathcal P}}\to0,$$
all supports have dimension at most zero. Euler additivity and the zero-support formula turn this into $b=\dim_k\Gamma(X,I_{E_{\mathcal P}}/\mathcal B)+|E_{\mathcal P}|\ge |E_{\mathcal P}|$. Coherence of the kernel follows from the coherence lemma; the finite reduced closed subscheme has coherent structure sheaf locally given by finite modules over Noetherian rings.

source.place: Proposition 2.17(ii), printed p.233, and Theorem 3.9 proof, printed p.247; length calculation by Stacks Tags 08AA and 0AYT

proof.text: Suppose $V=H^0(X,L)$. Every section $s\in V$ factors through the evaluation image: use the global element $s\otimes1$ of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X$. Thus it is a section of $L\otimes\mathcal B$. Conversely a section of this subsheaf is a section of $L$, and the inclusion is injective on sections. These two inclusions prove the claimed equality inside $H^0(X,L)$.

source.place: Theorem 3.9 proof, printed p.247, equality of section spaces after adjoining the base locus

proof.text:
Finally suppose $L=I_T\otimes\omega_X$ as in the statement. Locally $I_T=(t)$ with $t$ a nonzerodivisor. Multiplication $a\mapsto ta$ identifies $\mathcal O_X$ with $I_T$ on that open; hence $I_T$ is a line, and $I_T\otimes\mathcal B\to I_T\mathcal B$ is an isomorphism, given locally by $t\otimes a\mapsto ta$. The product is a coherent ideal (locally isomorphic to $\mathcal B$). Away from $T\cup Z$ it is the unit ideal, so its zero scheme $\bar T$ is zero-dimensional; the finite-subscheme node makes its length finite. Since $I_T\mathcal B\subseteq I_T$, it contains $T$. The coherent exact sequence is
$$0\to I_T/I_T\mathcal B\to\mathcal O_X/I_T\mathcal B\to\mathcal O_X/I_T\to0.$$
Locally multiplication by $t$ identifies its left term with $I_T\otimes(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal B)$. The zero-support formula, with the invertible module $I_T$, gives $\chi(X,I_T/I_T\mathcal B)=b$. Euler additivity and the same zero-support formula on the other two terms yield $\ell(\bar T)=\ell(T)+b$. The inclusions into $\omega_X$ agree locally with multiplication by $t$ and by elements of $\mathcal B$, so $I_{\bar T}\otimes\omega_X=L\otimes\mathcal B$ inside $L$. Step 5 now gives the final equality of canonical section subspaces. No Cartier property of $\bar T$ is asserted or used.
